header.goal: Build FOTW² (Fly On The Wall, squared) — a lightweight community-intelligence extension/cockpit for game devs and modders — from a GPT-authored spec in Google Drive into a working TypeScript monorepo, then evolve it toward a downloadable, tiered product that unites the user's other MCP 'wrenches' (ModWrench, DefWrench, MyneWrench).

decisions.decision: Port the Drive scaffold faithfully into the FlyOnWallWrench repo rather than rebuild from scratch.
decisions.rationale: Investigation showed a real, coherent pnpm/turbo TypeScript monorepo in Drive (core/adapters/mcp-server/web/extensions) that matched the docs; porting preserved the GPT-authored design and reached a working M0+M1 demo fastest.

decisions.decision: Reach the work surface via the connected Google Drive MCP; build/commit in the local cloned repos.
decisions.rationale: The sandbox cannot see the user's local G:\ drive, but a Drive API integration could read the files; the four repos were cloned into the container for git work.

decisions.decision: Architecture is pure-extension: run the 'brain' (core+adapters) bundled inside the side panel; no localhost server required.
decisions.rationale: Devs/modders juggle many tabs; an in-extension brain means no server to start, offline-capable, fewer moving parts. Web app demoted to optional team host.

decisions.decision: Side-panel nav is dynamic and selectable — sections = the user's connected sources, plus Ask/Pulse/Queue/Add/Settings/Rack tabs.
decisions.rationale: User wanted user-choice (1 source or 6), a live forum/Twitch-chat feel, and a targeted 'anyone else?' broadcast — selectability later doubles as the tiering mechanism.

decisions.decision: Posting is universal draft+paste (approval-gated), not auto-post.
decisions.rationale: Only method that works on every platform incl. Steam (no posting API); zero ban risk; the user is the one posting in their own session. Auto-post deferred to GitHub/Reddit only.

decisions.decision: Live reads ride the user's own logged-in page via DOM scraping (Plaid-style, no keys), reading only the active tab after a per-site Connect grant.
decisions.rationale: User explicitly wanted no held secrets; anchored host matchers reject spoof domains; avoids the bannable session-token/self-bot path.

decisions.decision: Design system: gunmetal + steel/slate/amber + copper-framed accent tabs + subtle terminal-green; WebGL aurora shader, liquid glass, living edges; subtle (not dramatic) pointer parallax.
decisions.rationale: User wanted game-dev/IDE common colors with a subtle hacker green, simple-but-powerful layout, and toned-down motion.

decisions.decision: Rebrand 'Help Me Comms' → FOTW² (real superscript ²) in user-facing strings only; keep internal command IDs / package names.
decisions.rationale: Cosmetic rename = zero build breakage; relicensing/renaming internals risks the build for no visible gain.

decisions.decision: Open-core licensing: MIT core (chat, adapters, WrenchBridge contract) + protected BUSL-1.1 packages/pro (the cross-wrench correlation spine) + commercial Studio/Team tier.
decisions.rationale: Protect the moat (the spine) from resale while keeping a forkable free base as the funnel; set the package boundary on the spine's first commit because relicensing public code later is legally messy.

decisions.decision: The moat is the cross-wrench correlation spine (community signal → mod cause → dev fix → creator impact), surfaced via 'The Rack' cockpit; wrenches are selectable/pairable.
decisions.rationale: Three wrenches are headless MCP servers; FOTW² is the only face. Threading one story across them is the defensible 'what the wrenches become together' — not co-located tabs.

decisions.decision: Build order: gameplan (STRATEGY.md) → license boundary → live spine → one-click installer.
decisions.rationale: Decide → prove → package; each step depends on the prior. Slot the license-boundary as step 1.5 so the spine lands in the right-licensed package from its first commit.

decisions.decision: Credential policy: OS keychain (default) → session-only → .env (beta last-resort only); extension + helper hold no secrets.
decisions.rationale: Matches the 'no keys on the wrenches' goal and the Chrome Web Store review/trust story; ModWrench already uses the OS keychain.

decisions.decision: Ship pre-built artifacts (extensions/browser/dist + help-me-comms.vsix) un-ignored in git for no-build install.
decisions.rationale: Non-GitHub humans must never see a terminal; load-unpacked / install-from-VSIX should work straight from a clone.

header.next_step: User to drag-test SnatchIt live in Chrome (verify the crop aligns with the drawn box; DPR/scroll-offset is the likely tweak). Then, per the gameplan, the license-key gate, then the signed double-click installer (.exe/.dmg bundling Node + auto-start the helper). Optional: wire a real wrench into the helper's 'mcp' mode to thread actual ModWrench/DefWrench data.
constraints: Sandbox egress is locked to the npm registry only — cannot reach discord.com/github.com/google etc.; live external-API and live-Discord proofs must run on the user's machine (scripts/prove-discord.mjs).
Cannot produce signed OS installers (.exe/.dmg) in-sandbox: no code-signing certs, no cross-platform build runners, cannot run GUI installers.
Cannot run a real browser to screenshot/click-test the extension; previews are hand-rendered SVGs and the live capture (SnatchIt) is untested in-sandbox.
A homoglyph corruption deterministically mangles base64 blobs containing 'dis'/'discord' and some JSON ('dist') on emission — use base64 -d self-checks or write source/JSON as plain heredocs.
Browser extension bundle cannot safely hold secrets — it stays on mock/session data by design; real API creds live server-side or in the OS vault.
GitHub MCP tools restricted to 171county/{flyonwallwrench,defwrench,mynewrench,modwrench}; develop on branch claude/dazzling-hamilton-MkAgB; push with -u and DCO sign-off.
Do not put the model identifier in commits/PRs/code; model is claude-opus-4-8.
do_not_relitigate: Architecture = pure extension with in-extension brain; web app demoted to optional team host (not the daily driver).
Posting = universal draft+paste/approval-gated; nothing auto-posts; Steam has no posting API.
Live reads = ride the user's own logged-in session/DOM, no held keys (Plaid-without-keys); reject the bannable self-bot path.
Licensing = open-core: MIT core + BUSL-1.1 packages/pro for the spine; WrenchBridge contract stays in MIT core for forkers.
The moat is the correlation spine, not the adapters or the UI.
Brand is FOTW² with a real superscript; internal IDs/package names left unchanged.
Palette is gunmetal/steel/slate/amber/copper with subtle terminal-green; parallax kept subtle (tilt 2deg / drift 6px).
Build order is gameplan → license boundary → live spine → one-click.
Lawyer gate: BUSL vs SSPL vs closed-Pro and the BUSL parameters require an IP attorney before any public relicense — placeholder LICENSE is intentional.
